title: Test headless Codex single-Action run, OpenCode on failure (experiment fixture)
problem: Agents cannot run the Codex or OpenCode CLIs: they fail inside the agent sandbox and launching unsandboxed agents is refused. So nobody knows whether a headless provider session, started with the unattended command line Arcadia's launcher builds for a standing-policy launch, can finish one trivial governed Action with no human input. A fingerprint launch today runs the interactive TUI, which never exits, so this has to be proved by running the provider for real, on a disposable fixture, as the operator.
desired_effect: In a fresh Decision 0082 experiment workspace and a one-Action fixture repository (no remote) under a temporary directory (the workspace lives in $TMPDIR, not workspaces/exp-*, because Codex's workspace-write sandbox can write the temp directory but not the workspaces directory, and everything is disposable and removed afterwards), Arcadia prepares the Action (go --apply --agent codex with a seeded immutable build packet and a fresh experiment-only heartbeat), then the script runs Codex headless with the exact unattended argv Arcadia's shipped launch builder produces (codex exec --json --model ... --config model_reasoning_effort=... --sandbox workspace-write --cd <worktree> <brief>) for at most 15 minutes, teeing its output to a log. It then prints and records a PASS/FAIL table: the provider exited 0 within the cap, MARKER.md has the exact expected line, node scripts/check-fixture.mjs passes, a clean commit with the exact file exists on the candidate branch (when the agent could not commit, as Codex's workspace-write sandbox denies Git's index.lock, the script plays the host's role afterwards with arcadia preserve's own code, then judges the commit), and a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask was drafted (preview accepts it) or settled by the agent itself (the Action is complete in the experiment database, the archived Ask's candidate revision is an ancestor of HEAD holding the exact file, and the tree is clean). It also reports whether the worktree's gitdir lies inside Codex's sandbox-writable roots and, as information only, what session reconcile makes of the finished Session (accepted_completion is unreachable in an experiment workspace because no worker exists). Only if Codex fails does it repeat the whole test on a fresh fixture with OpenCode (opencode run --model ...). Run it from /runs, or from a terminal: /Users/pmark/Dev/MR/Arcadia/arcadia/artifacts/generated/operator-scripts/test-headless-provider-single-action.sh run Expected duration: typically 2 to 10 minutes, at most about 35. Cost: uses your existing Codex (and only if Codex fails, OpenCode) plan; no separate spend. The receipt reports the agent part and the host part separately, so an agent-only pass is visible: PASS means the agent committed; PASS (agent + host preservation) means the host step committed; PASS (agent); host preservation not exercised means the agent did everything but the host step could not run in an experiment workspace.
preconditions: Run on the operator's own Mac, signed in: codex on PATH and codex login status succeeds (OpenCode: opencode on PATH and opencode auth list shows a credential, checked only if Codex fails)
Today is within Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18)
The Arcadia checkout this library belongs to has its dependencies installed (the test runs its CLI)
No other input is needed; nothing is read from or written to the live workspace except a read-only leak-check snapshot

Where it works: the experiment workspace, fixture and candidate worktree live in a temporary directory under $TMPDIR (not workspaces/exp-*), so the provider's sandbox can write them; the scripts' logs and receipt stay in runs/<timestamp-pid>/

parameters.--keep: Optional argument (terminal only; /runs passes none), or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1: keep the temporary experiment workspace, fixture and candidate worktree for inspection. The run logs and receipt are always kept.
parameters.ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: Optional environment variable: the per-provider cap in milliseconds (default 900000, fifteen minutes).

expected_duration: Typically 2 to 10 minutes. At most about 35 minutes: one 15-minute provider cap for Codex, one for OpenCode when Codex fails, plus about a minute of setup per provider.
cost_note: Uses the operator's existing Codex (and, only if Codex fails, OpenCode) plan: one short headless session each on a one-line task. No API key is read or entered and no separate spend is authorized or incurred.

does: Refuses before creating anything unless today is within Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18) and the codex binary is on PATH with codex login status succeeding; OpenCode, reached only if Codex fails, is refused only when opencode auth list clearly shows no credentials (an uncertain answer warns and proceeds)

Creates a temporary directory, a fresh experiment workspace in it with arcadia init --profile experiment, and a one-Action fixture repository with no remote under that workspace's projects directory; every Arcadia command names that workspace explicitly and the live workspace is never addressed

Writes a freshly timestamped worker heartbeat file inside the experiment workspace only (the experiment guard forbids starting a worker), seeds one immutable build packet there, and prepares the candidate worktree with go --apply through a recording process boundary that starts nothing

Runs the provider CLI headless with the unattended argv the shipped launch builder produces for go --launch, in the candidate worktree, with ARCADIA_WORKSPACE set in the provider's own environment to the experiment workspace (never exported in any shell) and the operator-script markers removed, for at most 15 minutes, killing its whole process group on timeout. The provider process is not confined to the fixture beyond what the provider enforces: Codex runs with --sandbox workspace-write, but OpenCode runs unsandboxed with its ambient permission configuration, so a misbehaving OpenCode could write anywhere the operator can; the 15-minute cap and process-group kill bound it, and the fixture holds nothing of value

Lets go --launch run its ordinary provider capacity probe, which for Codex is a real, read-only codex app-server account/rateLimits/read query against the operator's own Codex account, and which refreshes the local coding-agent telemetry cache under ~/.arcadia/telemetry (the one Arcadia-side write outside the temporary directory and runs/<timestamp-pid>/)

Takes a read-only live-workspace leak-check snapshot before and after. Other sessions legitimately write the live workspace, but Decision 0082 stops experiments at any experiment-caused write, so a difference is logged and receipted as LIVE WORKSPACE CHANGED: attribute before any further experiment

Writes run.log, one log per provider, a receipt.json (arcadia-operator-run-receipt-v1 with per-provider results and log paths) and, on failure, a failure-handoff.md under runs/<timestamp-pid>/, which are always kept
Removes the temporary directory at the end unless --keep or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1 is given

Lets the providers write their own normal session and state directories (for example under ~/.codex and ~/.local/share/opencode), as any run of them does; the script itself never reads or edits them. Codex also persists a project-trust entry, [projects."<fixture repo>"] trust_level = "trusted", to ~/.codex/config.toml for a new project directory: a read-only look at that file after operator run 20261009T135444Z-90379 found exactly such an entry for this test's fixture path. The Decision 0082 leak check reports it as a changed hashes.codexConfig. It is reported as a POSSIBLE Decision 0082 stop condition and never pre-attributed: the operator attributes it before any further experiment. To stop the experiment touching host config, the test passes Codex a per-invocation --config trust override (projects."<path>".trust_level="trusted") for exactly its own fixture repository and candidate worktree; whether Codex then skips the write is unverified until the next run's leak check

After the provider exits and the Session is reconciled, if the candidate is the exact MARKER.md left uncommitted beside a drafted Ask, runs arcadia preserve's own code (runPreserveCommand, the code the worker runs) on that experiment candidate: its manual-handoff path, which authorizes local preservation only (validation under Seatbelt in the temp dir, then a local commit), with no remote, push or pull request. It may refuse in an experiment workspace; that is reported, not forced. A step that ran and refused is reported as host_failed, one that could not run here as not_exercised, and a step that committed and then errored as preserved

Gives OpenCode, and only OpenCode, a per-process OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission grant (external_directory allow) for the temporary tree this test created, because OpenCode's non-interactive run auto-rejects permission prompts and its first tool call in the macOS temporary directory was refused (run 20261009T135444Z-90379); the operator's ~/.config/opencode is never read for this or written
never_does: Never addresses, reads for any purpose but the leak-check snapshot, or writes the live martianrover workspace, never exports ARCADIA_WORKSPACE, and gives the provider an arcadia shim that pins the experiment workspace and refuses to fall back to the default

Never activates production, starts, stops or restarts a service or worker, installs the go-broker, or merges, pushes or opens anything on GitHub, and never settles anything in the live workspace (the provider may settle its own completion Ask, but only inside the experiment workspace)

Never reads, edits or repairs provider global configuration or authentication (codex login, opencode auth login and their config files stay the operator's; the providers' own session and state directories are the only provider-side writes, made by the providers), and never installs software or enters a credential
Never registers a repository with a remote, and never touches the primary Arcadia checkout, other worktrees or any path outside its temporary directory and runs/<timestamp-pid>/
Never reports accepted_completion: with no worker in an experiment workspace it cannot be reached, so session reconcile output is information only

Never pushes, opens a pull request or touches a remote during the host step, and never runs the worker's leased preservation path with production authority; an experiment workspace cannot hold that authority

success.effect: At least one provider (Codex first) exited 0 within the cap, wrote and committed the expected MARKER.md, passed the fixture check and drafted a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask that preview accepts. The receipt records the table, the model, the exact command, the log paths and the gitdir finding. The receipt separates agentPart from hostPart and records passKind (agent, agent_and_host, agent_host_failed or agent_only).
success.next: Read receipt.json under runs/<timestamp-pid>/ in the operator-scripts directory. If Codex passed, headless Codex is viable for a standing-policy launch on this host; give the receipt (especially the gitdir finding) to Arcadia to decide the next Action. If only OpenCode passed, say so in the same handoff. If the receipt's liveWorkspaceSnapshot.changedDuringRun is true, attribute every change (other sessions versus this experiment) before any further experiment; an experiment-caused write is a Decision 0082 stop condition. Read hostPart: agent_only means the agent's work is proven but host preservation (the worker's commit step) still needs a real exercise, which an experiment workspace cannot give.

failure.effect: No provider passed every criterion, or a precondition refused. The script exits non-zero and writes receipt.json and failure-handoff.md with the table and the failing criterion for each provider, plus every provider log. Nothing outside the temporary directory and the run directory was changed.
failure.next: Give failure-handoff.md, run.log and the provider logs to a coding agent to diagnose the first failing criterion. A refusal names its precondition: sign in (codex login or opencode auth login), put the binary on PATH, or note that Decision 0082's window closed. Rerun with --keep from a terminal to inspect the fixture. If the log says LIVE WORKSPACE CHANGED, attribute the change before any further experiment. A Codex candidate left uncommitted is expected (its sandbox denies Git's index.lock); the host step or the agent-only fallback should cover it, so a FAIL on the commit criterion means something else is wrong. If the log says LIVE WORKSPACE CHANGED and names hashes.codexConfig, that is a possible Decision 0082 stop condition for the operator to attribute (Codex persists project-trust entries there).
